AK.reason: The corpus is Alaska Statutes Chapter 08.38 which directly licenses and regulates dietitians and nutritionists, including licensure requirements, disciplinary provisions, and definitions.

AL.reason: The corpus contains Alabama Code chapters 34-34, 34-34A, and 34-34B which directly license and regulate the practice of dietetics and nutrition, including qualifications, board creation, licensing procedures, and enforcement.

AR.reason: The corpus contains Arkansas Code Chapter 83 (Dietitians), which is the Dietetics Practice Act establishing licensing requirements, the Arkansas Dietetics Licensing Board, and regulations for the practice of dietetics.

AZ.reason: Section 36-416 only addresses hospital ordering authority for registered dietitians and does not contain a licensure law regulating the practice of dietetics/nutrition.

CA.reason: The corpus contains California law directly regulating registered dietitians and dietetic technicians, including qualifications, scope of practice, and supervised practice provisions.

CO.reason: The single section present (6-1-707) is a deceptive trade practices statute that merely restricts use of the title 'dietitian,' not a licensure/regulatory chapter that establishes a dietetics licensing scheme.

CT.reason: The corpus contains Connecticut General Statutes sections 20-206m through 20-206t, which directly establish the certification requirements, fees, renewal, disciplinary standards, and scope of practice for dietitian-nutritionists in Connecticut.

DE.reason: The corpus contains the full Delaware licensure law for dietitians/nutritionists including the Board, qualifications, licensure requirements, and disciplinary provisions under Chapter 38 sections 3801-3812.

FL.reason: The corpus contains Florida's Dietetics and Nutrition Practice Act (ss. 468.501-468.518) which directly licenses and regulates dietitians and nutritionists.

GA.reason: The corpus contains the full Georgia Dietetics Practice Act (Chapter 11A of Title 43) which explicitly licenses and regulates dietitians and dietetic practice.

HI.reason: Hawaii Revised Statutes Chapter 448B explicitly establishes a dietitian licensure program, defines licensed dietitian, sets licensure requirements, and provides enforcement provisions for the practice of dietetics.

IA.reason: Chapter 152A explicitly establishes licensure requirements for dietitians in Iowa, including definitions, license requirements, and exemptions.

ID.reason: The corpus contains Idaho Code chapter 54-35 which explicitly establishes licensure requirements, definitions, grounds for discipline, and penalties for dietitians in Idaho.

IL.reason: The corpus is the Illinois Dietitian Nutritionist Practice Act (225 ILCS 30), which directly licenses and regulates the practice of dietetics and nutrition in Illinois.

IN.reason: The corpus is Indiana Code Article 14.5 (Dietitians), which directly licenses and regulates the practice of dietetics/nutrition in Indiana.

KS.reason: The corpus contains the Kansas Dietitians Licensing Act (KSA 65-5901 through 65-5913), which directly licenses and regulates the practice of dietetics.

KY.reason: The corpus is Kentucky Revised Statutes Chapter 310, which directly licenses dietitians and certifies nutritionists, including definitions, licensure/certification requirements, board creation, and penalties.

LA.reason: The corpus contains the Louisiana Dietetics/Nutrition Practice Act of 1987 (RS 37:3081-3094), which directly licenses and regulates dietitians and nutritionists.

MA.reason: The corpus contains the full licensure law for dietitians/nutritionists in MA, covering board powers, application requirements, examinations, discipline, renewal, reciprocity, penalties, and address requirements.

MD.reason: The corpus is Maryland Health Occupations Title 5, which directly establishes the State Board of Dietetic Practice, defines the practice of dietetics, and sets licensure requirements for licensed dietitian-nutritionists.

ME.reason: The corpus contains Maine's complete dietetics licensure chapter (32 §§9901-9916) establishing the Board of Licensing of Dietetic Practice and licensing requirements for dietitians and dietetic technicians.

MI.reason: The corpus contains Michigan Public Health Code Part 183 sections explicitly licensing dietitian nutritionists, including definitions, license requirements, and qualified supervisor provisions for the practice of medical nutrition therapy.

MN.reason: The corpus contains MN sections 148.621-148.634 which directly establish the Board of Dietetics and Nutrition Practice, define dietitian and nutritionist, and set licensure requirements for those occupations.

MO.reason: The corpus contains the full Missouri Dietitian Practice Act (sections 324.200 to 324.225) which directly licenses and regulates the practice of dietetics/nutrition.

MS.reason: The corpus is the Mississippi Dietetics Practice Act (Chapter 73-10), which directly licenses and regulates dietitians and nutritionists in Mississippi.

MT.reason: Montana Title 37 Chapter 25 explicitly licenses and regulates nutritionists/dietitians including definitions, licensing requirements, scope of practice, and disciplinary provisions.

NC.reason: The corpus contains Article 25 of NC Chapter 90, the Dietetics/Nutrition Practice Act, which directly licenses and regulates dietitians and nutritionists in North Carolina.

ND.reason: The corpus contains North Dakota Century Code Chapter 43-44, which is the full dietetics/nutrition licensure law establishing the board, license requirements for licensed registered dietitians and licensed nutritionists, scope of practice, and related provisions.

NE.reason: The corpus includes the Uniform Credentialing Act which explicitly lists medical nutrition therapy as a credentialed practice (38-121(1)(w)) and references the Medical Nutrition Therapy Practice Act as one of the practice acts governed by this framework.

NH.reason: The corpus is NH RSA Chapter 326-H, the Dietitians Licensure Act, which directly licenses and regulates the practice of dietitians in New Hampshire.

NJ.reason: The corpus includes chapter 45:16B which covers the State Board of Dietetics and Nutrition, and the State Board of Dietetics and Nutrition is explicitly named in the shared administrative sections (45:1-3.1, 45:1-15) that apply to it, confirming the dietetics/nutrition licensure law is present.

NM.reason: The corpus contains the full Nutrition and Dietetics Practice Act (NMSA 61-7A-1 through 61-7A-15) which directly licenses and regulates dietitians, nutritionists, and nutrition associates in New Mexico.

NV.reason: The corpus is NRS Chapter 640E which directly licenses and regulates the practice of dietetics in Nevada, including definitions, licensure requirements, scope of practice, disciplinary provisions, and board authority.

NY.reason: The corpus contains NY Education Law Title VIII (Article 65 general provisions for licensed professions), which is the shared administrative/licensing framework under which dietetics/nutrition is licensed in NY, and the citation list covers 43 sections of this title that governs admission to and practice of all regulated professions including dietitians/nutritionists.

OH.reason: The corpus is Ohio Revised Code Chapter 4759, which directly licenses and regulates the practice of dietetics, including licensure requirements, fees, disciplinary provisions, and exemptions.

OK.reason: The corpus contains the full Licensed Dietitian Act (Oklahoma Title 59, sections 1721 onward) including licensure requirements, examination, renewal, discipline, and the Dietitian Licensure Compact.

OR.reason: The corpus contains Oregon Revised Statutes Chapter 691 which directly licenses and regulates dietitians, including definitions, licensure requirements, renewal, discipline, and the Board of Licensed Dietitians.

PA.reason: The corpus contains explicit dietitian-nutritionist licensure provisions including license requirements, examinations, renewal, and disciplinary procedures under the Pennsylvania Nursing Law as amended to include dietetics-nutrition practice.

RI.reason: The corpus contains Chapter 5-64, the Dietitian/Nutritionist Act, which directly licenses and regulates the practice of dietetics in Rhode Island, including licensure requirements, board structure, discipline, and enforcement.

SC.reason: The corpus is the South Carolina Dietetics Licensure Act (Chapter 20, Title 40) which directly licenses and regulates dietitians in South Carolina.

SD.reason: Chapter 36-10B explicitly licenses and regulates the practice of nutrition and dietetics in South Dakota, covering definitions, qualifications, application, renewal, discipline, and exemptions.

TN.reason: The corpus contains Tennessee Code Chapter 63-25, the Dietetics/Nutrition Practice Act, which directly licenses and regulates dietitians/nutritionists including licensure requirements, board creation, and disciplinary provisions.

TX.reason: The corpus is Texas Occupations Code Chapter 701, the Licensed Dietitian Act, which directly licenses and regulates the practice of dietetics/nutrition in Texas.

UT.reason: The corpus contains Utah Code Chapter 58-49 (Dietitian Certification Act) which directly licenses and regulates the practice of dietetics in Utah, including qualifications, certification, titles, and disciplinary provisions.

VA.reason: Section 54.1-2731 directly regulates who may hold themselves out as a dietitian or nutritionist, establishing the qualifications and requirements for that occupation in Virginia.

VT.reason: The corpus contains Vermont's dietitian certification law including definitions, eligibility, examination, application, renewal, and unprofessional conduct provisions directly regulating the practice of dietetics.

WA.reason: The corpus contains Washington RCW chapter 18.138, which directly establishes certification requirements and regulations for certified dietitians and certified nutritionists.

WI.reason: The corpus contains Wisconsin subchapter V of chapter 448 which directly licenses and regulates dietitians, including certification requirements, examinations, disciplinary proceedings, and the dietitian licensure compact.

WV.reason: The corpus is WV Code chapter 30-35, which directly establishes licensure requirements, a licensing board, fees, examinations, and penalties for the practice of dietetics/licensed dietitians in West Virginia.

WY.reason: The corpus is Wyoming Title 33 Chapter 47, the Dietetics Licensure Act, which directly licenses and regulates the practice of dietetics in Wyoming.
